page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn7i-c32g1.32xlarge is an x86_64 GPU-accelerated compute instance powered by Intel Xeon Platinum 8369B processors and NVIDIA Ampere A10 hardware accelerators. The system configuration comprises 128 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 64 physical cores operating at 2.9 GHz, supported by 48 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and AVX-512 VNNI vector instruction sets. Memory capacity totals 752.0 GB (approximately 5.88 GB per vCPU). Graphics and parallel processing tasks are accelerated by four NVIDIA A10 GPUs delivering 96 GB of aggregated VRAM (24 GB per GPU). It operates over a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 64 Gbps and contains no bundled local storage, requiring external cloud disks for persistent storage needs.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate top-tier parallel throughput enabled by the dense 128 vCPU count and high-speed memory interface. While single-core performance registers in the average bracket on the stress-ng benchmark at 1882.5, multi-core scaling shows strong metrics reaching 123935.69. Decompression throughput on bzip3 multi-threaded achieves 575.13 GB/sec, placing it within the top 10% of tested instances. The memory subsystem sustains 253.9 GB/sec read and 103.09 GB/sec write throughput for large uncached 256 MB blocks, accompanied by strong in-memory key-value processing capability reaching 100.72 million operations per second in Redis SET tests.

Given the density of four enterprise-grade Ampere GPUs and 752 GB RAM, the instance offers strong cost efficiency for GPU-intensive workloads compared to provisioning multiple smaller nodes. Potential architectural tradeoffs include the total absence of local NVMe storage and average single-thread baseline execution, meaning applications relying strictly on serial performance or low-latency local disk scratch space require network-attached storage architectures. The configuration is primarily tailored for distributed AI inference, graphics-intensive rendering pipelines, cloud visual computing, video processing, and high-throughput memory-resident data workloads.
